sections.history: Thalayalangadu, whose Tevaram name is Tiruthalaiyalankadu, lies about 15 km from Tiruvarur and some 8 km east of Kudavasal, in Tiruvarur district (Chimizhi post, via Sembangudi). It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirunavukkarasar (Appar). The stone temple is of the Chola period and later, and the lord bears the dance-names Nardhanapureeswarar and Aadavalleeswarar.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Nardhanapureeswarar — also Aadavallar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Balambikai, also called Tirumadanthai Ammai, in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The sacred tank is the Sangu Theertham, and the sthala vriksham is recorded variously as the vilva or the pala tree.
sections.legends: The lord's names Nardhanapureeswarar, 'lord of the city of dance,' and Aadavalleeswarar, 'the lord who is mighty in dance,' turn worship here toward Shiva as the cosmic dancer, Nataraja, whose dance sustains and dissolves the worlds. The goddess Balambikai, 'the youthful mother,' stands beside him. As with many smaller delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana is preserved chiefly in the local tradition and the Tevaram verses of Appar.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Thai new-moon day (January–February), Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March) and the Aippasi Annabhishekam (October–November), with Pradosha and Karthikai worship. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail near Kudavasal include Thalayalangadu among their stops.
sections.experience: At Thalayalangadu the pilgrim comes to a shrine whose names sing of dance. Before Nardhanapureeswarar, the lord of the city of dance, and the youthful Balambikai, beside the Sangu Theertham, the visitor feels the rhythm of Shiva Nataraja in a quiet Tevaram temple of the Kudavasal country.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Thalayalangadu is about 15 km from Tiruvarur and 8 km east of Kudavasal (Chimizhi post, via Sembangudi, PIN 612603), in Tiruvarur district. Kudavasal and Tiruvarur are the nearest rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
